key_insight: Structure-aware encoding reduction can reformulate a routing optimization problem to use far fewer qubits without changing the underlying objective.
engineering_relevance: For near-term quantum hardware, lowering qubit count and circuit complexity can materially improve solvability and make real-world optimization tasks more tractable.
method: Identify and exploit problem structure to reduce the encoding overhead.
Map latency-resilient routing with dual-link failures into a qubit-efficient formulation.
Compile and run the reduced model on trapped-ion hardware to compare against the benchmark.
evidence_signal: On the same trapped-ion quantum computer, the reduced formulation achieved a 100X improvement in success probability while also lowering qubit count and compiled circuit complexity.
watch_item: The improvement depends on how well the target problem structure matches the encoding reduction, so gains may not transfer uniformly to less structured instances.
paper_title: Encoding Matters: A Qubit-Efficient Reformulation for Quantum Resilient Routing
